nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show aRu0.250Ni with the form of nanoparticle clusters growing homogeneously on the Fe foam substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As revealed in SEM images (Figure 2b), aRu_{0.250}Ni with the form of nanoparticle clusters grows homogeneously on the Fe foam substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals average particle size of 13.46 nm with lattice fringes of 0.179 nm (200) and 0.205 nm (111) planes of metallic nickel, and 0.216 nm for Ru crystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of the prepared catalysts revealed an average particle size of 13.46 nm (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDX show high spatial correlation between Ru and Ni with Ru content of 26.13 at%, confirming homogeneous RuNi alloy formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM-EDX (Figure 2d) shows a high spatial correlation between the Ru and Ni, thus indicating the formation of homogeneous RuNi alloy with a Ru content of 26.13 at.%

properties.title: Eu 24.3 wt%, Re, Ni 7.58 wt%
properties.description: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy with elemental peaks

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD spectra show peaks shifted toward small angle compared to Ni, confirming successful Ru doping, with presence of Ru metal diffraction peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD spectra showed that aRu_{0.250} Ni was shifted toward a small angle compared to Ni (JCPDS No. 04-0850), confirming the successful doping of Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Ru and Ni; Ni 2p peaks at 852.7 eV (Ni^0 2p_{3/2}), 870.0 eV (Ni^0 2p_{1/2}), 855.8 eV (Ni^{2+}), 858.0 eV (Ni^{3+}); Ru 3p peaks at 463.08 eV (Ru^0) and 466.28 eV (Ru^{3+}).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In XPS spectra of the Ni 2p (Figure 3c), the peaks at 852.7 and 870.0 eV can be ascribed to the Ni^0 2p_{3/2} and Ni^0 2p_{1/2} orbitals, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV used to calculate double layer capacitance C_dl of 166.7 mF cm^{-2}, corresponding to ECSA of 3676 cm^2 for aRu0.250Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: C_dl calculated with cyclic voltammetry (CV) data (Figure 4c; Figure S16, Supporting Information) shows that the electrochemically active area of aRu_{0.250}Ni (166.7mFcm^{-2}) higher than aRu0Ni (90.5mFcm^{-2})

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show charge transfer resistance R_ct of 5.13 Ω for aRu0.250Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist plots (Figure 4e) and equivalent circuit diagrams (Table S2, Supporting Information) indicate R_ct of aRu_{0.250}Ni is only 5.13 Ω

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP confirms Ru doping level in aRu0.250Ni prepared from 10 mM Ru^{3+} and 50 mM Ni^{2+} electrolyte.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru doping level in the electrodes prepared from electrolytes with different Ru^{3+} concentrations was measured by ICP and the results indicated that aRu0.250Ni was prepared when the electrolyte had a Ru^{3+} concentration of 10 mM

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP measurement of Ru doping level confirms aRu0.250Ni composition from 10 mM Ru^{3+}, 50 mM Ni^{2+} electrolyte (Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru doping level in the electrodes prepared from electrolytes with different Ru^{3+} concentrations was measured by ICP and the results indicated that aRu0.250Ni was prepared when the electrolyte had a Ru^{3+} concentration of 10 mM and a Ni^{2+} concentration of 50 mM (Table S1, Supporting Information).
